Gion Festivals (祇園祭) and '''Tenno Festivals (Tennōsai''' 天王祭) are festivals held at [[Gion shrines|Gion Shrines]] and {{ill|Tenno Shrine|ja|天王神社}} shrines dedicated to [[Gozu Tennō]] (牛頭天王). Gozu Tennō has been syncretized with Japan's [[Susanoo-no-Mikoto|Susanoo]], and related legends and customs are found throughout Japan. They are the festivals of the [[Gion Faith|Gion cult]]

The Gion Festival, especially its elements related to {{ill|Matsuri float|en|Matsuri float|qid=Q11470974|lt=yamahoko processions}} and {{ill|Hayashi (music)|en|Hayashi (music)|qid=Q4171186|lt=Hayashi music}}, represents the most glamorous festival conducted by the {{ill|machishū|ja|町衆}} and {{ill|Chōnin|en|Chōnin|qid=Q115847|lt=chōnin}} classes in the {{ill|metropolitan prefecture|ja|都|lt=capital|3=都|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q124313007}}. This strong influence has spread widely to local festivals across Japan, particularly those held in {{ill|Jōkamachi|en|Jōkamachi|qid=Q909458|lt=Jōkamachi}} and conducted by chōnin. Additionally, the name "Gion Festival" itself has been widely adopted as a name for festivals held at shrines and temples dedicated to deities such as {{ill|Gozu Tennō|en|Gozu Tennō|qid=Q11570247|lt=Gozu Tennō}} and {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|en|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|qid=Q272993|lt=Susanoo-no-Mikoto}}, as well as summer festivals in general.

== [[:ja:祇園祭#日本全国の祇園祭|Major Gion Festivals Across Japan]] ==

Given the overwhelming number of festivals dedicated to the same deities or influenced by the Gion Festival, listing them comprehensively is not practical. This section highlights a selection of festivals bearing the Gion Festival name or strongly influenced by it. For festivals related to {{ill|Gozu Tennō|en|Gozu Tennō|qid=Q11570247|lt=Gozu Tennō}} or Susanoo, see {{ill|Gion and Tenno Festivals|ja|天王祭|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q17221495}}. For specific influences of the Gion Festival, refer to articles about local festivals.
